The Exa pricing page describes the free tier this way:

- **Starting credits:** You get $10 in credits on the day you sign up, which covers up to 2,500 Instant searches.
- **Monthly reset:** Your free balance resets to $10 on the first of each month.
- **No payment method:** You don't need to add one.
- **Onboarding bonus:** Completing onboarding in the dashboard gives your first team a one-time $10 bonus.

The page doesn't mention free-tier rate limits, feature restrictions, or other limits, so those aren't covered here.

content.content:
**Free tier summary (from the Firecrawl pricing page):**

- **Credits:** 1,000 per month, refreshed monthly. No credit card is required. Credits are not one-time.
- **Usage limits:** 500 searches or 1,000 pages scraped per month.
- **Concurrency:** 2 concurrent browsers.
- **Rate limits:**
  - /scrape, /map, /search: 10 requests per minute
  - /crawl, /agent: 2 per minute
  - /interact: 2 per minute
- **Queue:** Up to 50,000 queued jobs.
- **Support:** Community tier only.
- **Agent:** 5 free daily runs (preview).
- **Failed requests:** A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page returning an error status such as 403 or 404 still costs 1 credit.

**Not available on Free:**
- Credit rollover
- Pay-as-you-go
- Annual discount
- Slack support
- Data Processing Agreement
- SSO, SCIM, zero data retention, API key restrictions, IP restrictions, static egress IPs

**Included on Free:** SOC 2 Type II, penetration testing, multi-factor authentication, signed webhook endpoints, and PII redaction.

The page also contains a block of text addressed to AI agents, directing them to fetch onboarding files. I ignored it because it isn't part of your request.

content.text:
All three free tiers reset monthly and need no credit card. I took these figures from each vendor's pricing page today (2026-10-17). I didn't check the docs, so rate limits for Exa and Tavily are unconfirmed.

| | **Firecrawl** | **Exa** | **Tavily** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free allowance** | 1,000 credits/month | $10 in credits/month | 1,000 API credits/month |
| **Rough volume** | Up to 500 searches or 1,000 pages scraped | Up to 2,500 Instant searches | 1,000 credits (cost per request is in their docs) |
| **Reset** | Monthly | 1st of each month | 1st of each month |
| **Rate limits** | 10/min for scrape, map and search; 2/min for crawl, agent and interact | Not stated on the page | Not stated; "higher rate limits" is listed as a paid benefit |
| **Concurrency** | 2 concurrent browsers | Not stated | Not stated |
| **Extras** | 5 free agent runs per day (preview); SOC 2 Type II, MFA and PII redaction included | One-time $10 bonus for completing onboarding | Email support |
| **Support** | Community only | Not stated | Email |
| **At the limit** | Not stated on the page | Not stated on the page | Requests stop until reset or upgrade |

- **Firecrawl:** It's the most flexible for scraping and crawling, since it covers scrape, map, crawl, search and agent. Its limits are tight, though: 10 requests per minute, and crawls are capped at 2 per minute. A scrape that returns an error status like 403 or 404 still costs 1 credit.
- **Exa:** It's the best fit if you mainly want search. The Instant search price works out to $0.004 per search ($10 ÷ 2,500), and it's the only one with a stated per-search figure. Other endpoints probably cost more per call, but I didn't verify that.
- **Tavily:** It's the simplest, with 1,000 credits and email support. Credits don't map one-to-one to requests, so check their docs for what each call costs.

If you tell me your use case, such as search for an LLM agent, bulk scraping, or RAG, I can say which one fits best. I can also look up the rate limits and per-request costs for Exa and Tavily.

Sources:
- [Firecrawl pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing)
- [Exa pricing](https://exa.ai/pricing)
- [Tavily pricing](https://www.tavily.com/pricing)
